issue.title: Global plugins class loader should not be parent of project classloader
issue.body:
Global plugins are merged in with a build projects classpath (I mean, the sbt project build, that thing configure by `project/plugins.sbt`, not the applications build).  But in addition to this, the global plugins are loaded into their own classloader, and then this classloader is used as the parent of the build project.  This means that while it is possible for a projects build to override dependencies defined globally (eg, if a project declares a dependency in a never version of a library than is brought in by the global plugins) and ivy should work this out, because the global plugins are also in a parent classloader and classloading is parent first, such configuration has no affect.

This bites in practice when you have, for example, the sbt-idea plugin configured globally (a common use case), and it depends on commons-io 2.0.1, but then you have a plugin configured for a project (eg play) which depends on commons-io 2.4 and uses methods from commons-io 2.4 that aren't in 2.0.1.  Ivy resolves this nicely, evicting the 2.0.1 dependency from the sbt projects build, but then since the parent classloader just has the sbt-idea plugin, the commons-io 2.0.1 jar is still in that classloader, and because it's the parent the classes are loaded from there in preference to the 2.4 jar in the child classloader.

I can't see any reason why the global plugins should be in a parent classloader of the sbt project build, it seems this will only cause major problems.

I'm seeing this in 0.13.5-RC3, but we've only just added the commons-io dependency to play, so this may have existed for a long time.

body:
Work around is to add the following to `~/.sbt/0.13/plugins/build.sbt`:

```
libraryDependencies += "commons-io" % "commons-io" % "2.4"
```

issue.title: Reduce size of PlayIO API

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
- Inline some methods into the Files API
- Always close when reading a stream
- Didn't use scala.io.Source because it doesn't really support reading binary data and because it looks slow, which wouldn't be great for some use cases, e.g. reading assets or when a user uses Files.readFile.

issue.title: Remove RouterIO and replace with commons-io

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
This gives Play a build-time dependency on commons-io, but not a runtime dependency.

Needs to be backported to 2.3.x.

issue.title: Downgrade commons-io dependency so that it's compatible with sbt-idea

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
Fixes #2882.

When sbt-idea is a global plugin it brings in an old version of commons-io. This change downgrades Play's version to match sbt-idea's version so that Play's sbt-plugin and sbt-idea can run in the same classloader as each other.
